# Chart decision tree

Choose a chart in three steps, in this order. The tree starts from **what is in the data**, because that can be read from the columns, then asks **what the reader should see**, then gives a chart to **start with** and the conditions under which to **go further** to a richer form. Color comes last, from what it has to encode. [choosing-a-chart.md](choosing-a-chart.md) is the same advice by question type, and the cookbook page of each chart has its spec and code.

In Python, `mv.suggest(df)` reads the table, places it in this tree, checks every condition against the data and prints the result. Check how it read the columns, and pass `category=`, `measure=`, `size=` or `time=` when a guess is wrong.

**Start with** is right when no condition holds: it is the chart most readers decode fastest. When a condition holds, the richer chart usually says more; use it when it answers the question better, and say which condition you used in the chart brief:

```
Path:   <shape> -> <question type> -> <chart> (start, or go further: <condition>)
Color:  <pattern> (<why>)
```

## 1. What is in the data?

| Shape | Looks like |
|---|---|
| [One number, or a few](#single) | A single row, or a handful of headline figures. |
| [One measure per person or team (many rows)](#people) | Many rows, one per person or team, with a measure (compa-ratio, span of control, tenure) and maybe a group column. |
| [Categories × one measure](#cat-measure) | One row per category (job family, site, role) with a measure, maybe a count column and a benchmark. |
| [Parts of a whole](#composition) | Columns that add up to 100 (or to a total) in every row: workforce mix, survey favorability, time mix. |
| [A bridge from one total to another](#bridge) | Steps with a kind column (total, delta): headcount bridge, labor cost bridge. |
| [A pair of values per category](#pairs) | Before and after (rank_2023 and rank_2026, FY25 and FY26) or us and them (internal and market pay) for each category, or a period column with two values. |
| [Categories × several measures](#cat-measures) | One row per category with two or more measures in different units (a scorecard; pay vs. exposure). |
| [Two sets of categories × one measure](#matrix) | A long table: business unit × driver, function × quarter, with one value per pair. |
| [A measure over time](#time) | A period column (months, quarters, years) with three or more periods, maybe a series column. |
| [Flows from one state to another](#flows) | From and to columns with a count: internal moves, pipeline stages. |
| [Places](#geo) | A state, country, county or FIPS column. |
| [Plans and status](#plans) | Workstreams with start and end dates, milestones, owners or a status column. |
| [Overlapping groups](#sets) | Yes/no (1/0) membership columns with a count per combination. |

## 2–3. What should the reader see, and which chart?

<a id="single"></a>
### One number, or a few

A single row, or a handful of headline figures.

**What one figure should they remember?** (single number)

- **Start with:** [Big number with a comparison](cookbook/kpi-big-number.md) (`mv.kpi_card`)
- **Go further** when a target or goal to compare against: [Progress bar or ring toward the target](cookbook/kpi-big-number.md) (`mv.kpi_card(..., target=, ring_value=)`)
- **Go further** when several headline numbers side by side: [KPI row](cookbook/kpi-big-number.md) (`mv.kpi_row`)
- **Avoid:** Speedometers
- **Color:** Focus (default)

<a id="people"></a>
### One measure per person or team (many rows)

Many rows, one per person or team, with a measure (compa-ratio, span of control, tenure) and maybe a group column.

**How spread out is it? What's typical? Where are the outliers?** (distribution)

- **Start with:** [Strip plot or histogram](cookbook/distribution.md)
- **Go further** when people fall into 3 to 8 groups: [Strip or box plot by group, the focus group in blue](cookbook/distribution.md)
- **Avoid:** An average with no spread
- **Color:** Focus (default)

<a id="cat-measure"></a>
### Categories × one measure

One row per category (job family, site, role) with a measure, maybe a count column and a benchmark.

**Which is biggest, and by how much? How do they rank?** (magnitude / ranking)

- **Start with:** [Sorted bar](cookbook/bar.md) (`ax.barh + mv.highlight + mv.label_bars`)
- **Go further** when values bunched far from zero (the smallest is more than half the largest): [Dot plot](cookbook/dot-plot-dumbbell.md): bars must start at zero, which hides small differences
- **Go further** when the largest value is more than 20 times the smallest: [Proportional bubbles, or split the chart](cookbook/bubble-chart.md)
- **Go further** when more than 12 categories: [Sorted bar with the tail grouped into Other](cookbook/bar.md)
- **Go further** when a count column (headcount, employees, moves) whose values differ a lot (largest at least 5 times the smallest): [Bubble strip: position = the measure, bubble area = the count](cookbook/distribution.md): shows how close the categories are and how many people each one covers
- **Go further** when more than 20 categories: [Bubble strip with only the outliers and largest named](cookbook/distribution.md)
- **Avoid:** Rainbow, 3D or cut-off bars
- **Color:** Focus (default)

**How far is each from the benchmark?** (deviation) *(when there is a benchmark: a column that is the same on every row, one named target / benchmark / average, or a Total row)*

- **Start with:** [Diverging bars around the benchmark](cookbook/bar.md) (`mv.diverging_bars`)
- **Go further** when values bunched far from zero (the smallest is more than half the largest): [Dot plot with a labelled benchmark line](cookbook/dot-plot-dumbbell.md)
- **Avoid:** A benchmark nobody can see
- **Color:** Diverging

**Where is the most of it in absolute terms (rate × people)?** (magnitude (derived count)) *(when there is the measure is a rate or share and there is a count column, so rate × count gives an absolute amount)*

- **Start with:** [Sorted bar of the derived count, footnoted as an estimate](cookbook/bar.md) (`ax.barh + mv.highlight`)
- **Go further** when a count column (headcount, employees, moves) whose values differ a lot (largest at least 5 times the smallest): [Treemap: tile area = the count, shade = the rate](cookbook/treemap.md): people and the rate in one picture
- **Avoid:** A derived count presented as a recorded one
- **Color:** Focus (default)

<a id="composition"></a>
### Parts of a whole

Columns that add up to 100 (or to a total) in every row: workforce mix, survey favorability, time mix.

**What is each made of, and how do the mixes compare?** (part-to-whole)

- **Start with:** [100% stacked bar](cookbook/stacked-bar.md) (`mv.hstack`)
- **Go further** when only one row (a single whole): [One 100% bar, or a donut with 5 slices or fewer](cookbook/donut-pie.md) (`mv.hstack`)
- **Go further** when more than 5 parts: [Treemap, or group the small parts into Other](cookbook/treemap.md)
- **Go further** when the parts have a natural order (bands, ratings, unfavorable to favorable): [100% stacked bar in sequential shades (diverging for unfavorable to favorable)](cookbook/stacked-bar.md) (`mv.hstack(..., colors=...)`)
- **Avoid:** Pies over 5 slices
- **Color:** Categorical; Story segment + greys when one part is the story; Sequential when the parts have a natural order (bands, ratings, unfavorable to favorable)

<a id="bridge"></a>
### A bridge from one total to another

Steps with a kind column (total, delta): headcount bridge, labor cost bridge.

**What moved the total from A to B?** (part-to-whole (change))

- **Start with:** [Waterfall](cookbook/waterfall.md) (`mv.waterfall`)
- **Avoid:** Two stacked bars side by side
- **Color:** Focus (default)

<a id="pairs"></a>
### A pair of values per category

Before and after (rank_2023 and rank_2026, FY25 and FY26) or us and them (internal and market pay) for each category, or a period column with two values.

**What changed for each, or how big is each gap?** (change / comparison)

- **Start with:** [Dumbbell (before grey, after blue)](cookbook/dot-plot-dumbbell.md) (`mv.dumbbell`)
- **Go further** when the values are ranks: [Slope chart of the ranks](cookbook/slope-bump.md) (`mv.rank_slope`)
- **Go further** when 6 or fewer categories: [Slope chart](cookbook/slope-bump.md) (`mv.rank_slope`)
- **Go further** when the difference itself is the story (a gap column, or the pair is us vs. a benchmark): [Diverging bars of the difference](cookbook/bar.md) (`mv.diverging_bars`)
- **Go further** when a target or goal to compare against: [Dumbbell with a target line](cookbook/dot-plot-dumbbell.md) (`mv.dumbbell`)
- **Avoid:** Two separate bar charts the reader must compare
- **Color:** Focus (default)

<a id="cat-measures"></a>
### Categories × several measures

One row per category with two or more measures in different units (a scorecard; pay vs. exposure).

**Do two measures move together?** (correlation)

- **Start with:** [Scatter; bubble scatter when a count can be the bubble area](cookbook/scatter-bubble.md) (`mv.label_points`)
- **Go further** when 6 or fewer categories: [Two aligned bar charts, one per measure](cookbook/bar.md)
- **Avoid:** Dual axes
- **Color:** Focus (default)

**How does each category score across all the measures?** (ranking (profile))

- **Start with:** [Heat table (scorecard)](cookbook/tables.md) (`mv.heat`)
- **Go further** when more than 12 categories: [Parallel coordinates, the focus line in blue](cookbook/parallel-coordinates.md)
- **Avoid:** A clustered bar per measure
- **Color:** Sequential

<a id="matrix"></a>
### Two sets of categories × one measure

A long table: business unit × driver, function × quarter, with one value per pair.

**Where are the hot spots across both dimensions?** (correlation (two categories))

- **Start with:** [Heat table](cookbook/heatmap.md) (`mv.heat`)
- **Go further** when a benchmark: a column that is the same on every row, one named target / benchmark / average, or a Total row: [Diverging heat table around the benchmark](cookbook/heatmap.md) (`mv.heat(kind='diverging')`)
- **Avoid:** A rainbow color scale
- **Color:** Sequential; Diverging when values centered on zero or a target

<a id="time"></a>
### A measure over time

A period column (months, quarters, years) with three or more periods, maybe a series column.

**How is it moving? When did it change?** (change over time)

- **Start with:** [Line, the focus series in blue and the rest grey](cookbook/line.md) (`mv.label_line_ends`)
- **Go further** when more than 4 series: [Small multiples on one shared scale](cookbook/small-multiples.md) (`mv.multiples`)
- **Go further** when the measures are parts that add up to 100 in each period: [Stacked area, or 100% columns for a few periods](cookbook/stacked-area.md)
- **Go further** when two measures in different units over the same periods: [Two aligned panels (never dual axes)](cookbook/dual-axis.md)
- **Go further** when a target or goal to compare against: [Line with a labelled target line](cookbook/line.md)
- **Avoid:** Ten colored lines
- **Color:** Focus (default); Categorical when the measures are parts that add up to 100 in each period

<a id="flows"></a>
### Flows from one state to another

From and to columns with a count: internal moves, pipeline stages.

**Where do people go, and how many?** (relationships and flows)

- **Start with:** [Sankey](cookbook/sankey.md)
- **Avoid:** A color per stage
- **Color:** Focus (default); Ordered steps when the stages are a process in order

<a id="geo"></a>
### Places

A state, country, county or FIPS column.

**Where is it? Does place matter?** (geo-spatial)

- **Start with:** [Choropleth for rates](cookbook/maps.md) (`mckviz.geo`)
- **Go further** when the values are counts, not rates: [Bubble map (counts never go on a choropleth)](cookbook/maps.md) (`mckviz.geo`)
- **Avoid:** Counts on a choropleth
- **Color:** Sequential

<a id="plans"></a>
### Plans and status

Workstreams with start and end dates, milestones, owners or a status column.

**What happens when, who owns it, and is it on track?** (plans and status)

- **Start with:** [Roadmap (Gantt bars, milestones as markers)](cookbook/plans-status.md) (`mv.roadmap`)
- **Go further** when status recorded period by period: [Initiative tracker with a status column](cookbook/plans-status.md) (`mv.tracker`)
- **Avoid:** Red/amber/green by color alone
- **Color:** Status only

<a id="sets"></a>
### Overlapping groups

Yes/no (1/0) membership columns with a count per combination.

**How much do the groups overlap?** (relationships)

- **Start with:** [Venn, 3 sets at most](cookbook/venn.md)
- **Go further** when more than 3 sets: [Sorted bar of the combinations](cookbook/bar.md)
- **Avoid:** A Venn with 4 or more sets
- **Color:** Focus (default)

## 4. What does color encode?

Grey first, then color only the point. Pick the pattern from what the color has to say:

| Pattern | Use when | In mckviz |
|---|---|---|
| **Focus (default)** | The headline names one or two items: everything grey, those items McKesson Blue. Highlight at most two; bold the matching labels. | `mv.highlight(labels, focus=...)` |
| **Uniform + accent** | Every item belongs to the same story and one exception must pop: the series light blue, the exception navy. | `mv.highlight(labels, accent=..., base=C.focus_light)` |
| **Focus + accent** | A blue group the headline names plus one navy exception on grey context. Use sparingly. | `mv.highlight(labels, focus=..., accent=...)` |
| **Story segment + greys** | One part of a whole is the story: that segment blue on the baseline, the other parts in context greys. | `mv.hstack(..., story=...)` |
| **Categorical** | Every series or part matters and must be told apart: at most 6, always in the fixed order (blue, navy, bright blue, teal, mint, orange); prefer 4 or fewer. | `mv.categorical(n), or mv.hstack(..., colors=mv.categorical(n))` |
| **Sequential** | One ordered measure or ordered bands (low to high, bands of a rate): light to dark in one hue. Darker means more. | `mv.SEQUENTIAL['blue'], mv.sequential_cmap()` |
| **Diverging** | Values centered on zero or a target: orange below (worse), blue above, a neutral middle. | `mv.DIVERGING, mv.diverging_cmap(), mv.diverging_bars(...)` |
| **Ordered steps** | Process stages in order (blue to green), never for magnitude. | `mv.STEPS` |
| **Status only** | On track / at risk / off track / not started / done, always with a symbol and a word, never on data series. | `mv.STATUS, mv.status(...)` |

The hex values of every role are in [rules.md](rules.md); [color.md](color.md) has the reasoning.
